question: What is the best packaging experiment framework to test pricing without cannibalizing tiers?
answer:
## Pricing Packaging Experiment Framework Packaging—*which features bundled together*—influences price perception more than feature count. Pavilion case study: 2 identical feature sets packaged as "3 bundles" vs. "7 bundles" showed **19%** higher ASP on the 3-bundle version. Fewer options = less buyer fatigue = higher tier selection. Goal: Test new packaging (features regrouped, names changed, pricing adjusted) without eroding existing tier revenue. **Core rule: Run experiments in parallel, not sequential.** Sequential ("kill old packaging, roll new") = guaranteed cannibalization and churn. **Parallel Test Framework (8-Week Minimum):** **Weeks 1–2: Segment Selection & Hypothesis** Define 3–4 test cells: | Cell | % of New Signups | Packaging Model | Hypothesis | |------|-----------------|-----------------|----------| | Control | 40% | Current (3 tiers) | Baseline | | Experiment A | 20% | Feature-based (5 tiers) | More granularity → higher ASP | | Experiment B | 20% | Use-case based (3 tiers) | Clarity → faster conversion | | Experiment C | 20% | Hybrid (usage + seats) | Expansion capture → higher LTV | Key: **Only new signups** flow into experiments. Existing customers stay on current packaging. This prevents account disruption and churn. **Weeks 3–6: Volume Collection** Minimum sample per cell: - **100 conversions per cell** (if your monthly new customer flow is 500, this takes 5–8 weeks) - If you convert 20% of trials, you need 500 trials per cell = 2,000 total trials - **Stop early if**: One cell has 5x churn vs. control (signal failure) or data shows strong statistical significance (95% confidence) before week 8 **Weeks 7–8: Analysis & Rollout Decision** Metrics to track (per cell): | Metric | Weight | Control Baseline | Win Condition | |--------|--------|-----------------|---------------| | Conversion rate (trial → paid) | 25% | 25% | >28% | | ASP (average selling price) | 30% | $120 | >$130 | | CAC payback (months) | 20% | 14 months | <13 months | | 90-day net retention | 15% | 105% | >108% | | Churn rate (first 3 months) | 10% | 8% | <10% | **Success criteria**: To roll an experiment to 100% of signups, it must beat control on **2 of 3 primary metrics** (conversion, ASP, payback). If Experiment A wins on conversion (+3%) but loses on ASP (–$8), don't roll it yet. Hybrid: roll Experiment A to 60% of signups while keeping control at 40%; monitor 90-day retention. If it holds, migrate fully at week 12. **Cannibalization Prevention Checklist:** 1. **Price floor per tier**: Ensure new packaging tiers don't undercut existing pricing. - Old: Starter $99, Pro $299, Enterprise custom - New (Exp B): Use-case tier 1 $99, tier 2 $249, tier 3 $399 - Risk: Tier 2 at $249 under-prices Pro feature set. **Mitigate**: Ensure tier 2 has fewer features than old Pro, or lock tier 2 to 1-use-case only. 2. **Feature clarity**: Don't add features to lower tiers mid-test. If you discover a quick feature win during weeks 3–6, **resist** adding it. Document for post-test rollout. Adding features mid-test pollutes data. 3. **Sales team consistency**: Brief sales on all 4 packaging models. If they push only control or experiment A, data is skewed. Rotation: each AE pitches 2 of the 4 packaging models randomly. 4. **Contract term parity**: Offer 1-year, 2-year, 3-year terms *identically* across all cells. If control gets annual discount but Exp A gets monthly-only, ASP gap is artificial. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[New Signups] B{Random Assign

Results: - **Control** (3-tier): 22% conversion, $135 ASP, 14.2 month payback - **Experiment** (5-tier): 24% conversion (+2%), $142 ASP (+$7), 13.8 month payback (–0.4mo) - **90-day retention**: Both 106% (no difference) Decision: Roll 5-tier to 70% of new signups. Why only 70%? The +$7 ASP and +2% conversion are gains, but neither is *transformative*. Keep control at 30% as safety net. If 90-day retention on 5-tier drops below 103% by week 16, rollback. Result 12 weeks later: 5-tier cohort hit 104% 90-day retention (acceptable). Full rollout approved. **Annual ARR lift: +$180K** (600 new customers/year × $7 ASP improvement × 12 months). **MEDDPICC-Aligned Approach (CRO Playbook):** 1. **Metrics** (Decision criteria): Define wins before experiment starts 2. **Economic Buyer** (Pricing power): Test on tier most economically exposed (usually mid-market tier; enterprise is too noisy) 3. **Decision** (Rollout rule): 2 of 3 metrics beat control = rollout; otherwise iterate 4. **Discount** (Messaging): Each packaging variant needs internally-consistent discount logic (don't discount tier 2 without tier 1 discount) 5. **Paper Process** (Data rigor): Document every signup's cell assignment, cohort, tier chosen, conversion date, CAC, LTV 6. **Identify Impact** (Financial outcome): Calculate lift per cell; multiply by annual new customer volume 7. **Champion** (Ownership): Assign one person (RevOps) to track daily cohort performance and escalate early warning signs **CRO 8-week action plan:** Week 1: Define 3 packaging hypotheses based on sales objections (e.g., "customers say 'I only need X'—test a tier focused on X"). Week 2: Build pricing calculator showing all 4 packaging models side-by-side. Randomize cell assignment at signup. Week 3–6: Daily Slack alert if any cell conversion drops >30% vs. baseline. Sales huddle weekly to discuss feedback. Week 7: Interim analysis at 50 conversions per cell. Early signal of winner? Week 8: Final analysis. Roll winner to 70–100% based on confidence.
